title: Settlement of Promotional Interest Owed on a Closed Statement Cycle
content:
### 1. The promotional basis

Promotional interest owed on a savings or money market account of Savings & Money Market Accounts for a closed statement cycle is settled on the promotional basis, which is the account's qualifying new money for the three calendar months ending on the correction date less the withdrawals offset for that window, taken as no less than zero and no more than the tier's promotional balance cap.

### 2. Qualifying new money

Qualifying new money is the total of the deposits posted in those three calendar months other than internal transfers and automatic transfers from another Piedmont Crescent Bank account.

### 3. The withdrawals offset

Every withdrawal posted in those three calendar months is offset in full.

### 4. The yield and the accrual span

The promotional basis earns the tier's promotional annual percentage yield, and the accrual span is the 31 days of the closed statement month.

### 5. The promotional interest owed

The promotional interest owed is the promotional basis multiplied by the yield that applies, divided by 100, multiplied by the accrual span in days and divided by the day count basis of 365, and that figure is rounded half up to the cent.

### 6. The correction booked

The promotional interest already credited on the account in the one calendar month ending on the correction date is then deducted from it, and the correction booked is the remainder, taken as no less than zero.

### Worked figure on hypothetical inputs

Take a money market account whose records show, for the three calendar months ending on the correction date, deposits of 40000.00 USD of which 5000.00 USD arrived as an internal transfer from another Piedmont Crescent Bank account, withdrawals of 3000.00 USD, and a promotional interest credit of 10.00 USD in the one calendar month ending on that date. Take a hypothetical promotional annual percentage yield of 2.00 percent and a promotional balance cap well above the figures below.

Qualifying new money is 40000.00 USD less the 5000.00 USD internal transfer, that is 35000.00 USD. The withdrawals offset is the whole 3000.00 USD. The promotional basis is 35000.00 USD less 3000.00 USD, that is 32000.00 USD, which is neither below zero nor above the cap.

The promotional interest owed is 32000.00 USD multiplied by 2.00, divided by 100, multiplied by 31 and divided by 365, which is 54.3561 and rounds half up to 54.36 USD.

The correction booked is 54.36 USD less the 10.00 USD already credited, that is 44.36 USD.
